# assoc.pmi { #polars_corpus.assoc.pmi }

```python
assoc.pmi(f12, f1, f2, n)
```

Compute Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) for contingency table data.

Calculates PMI values measuring the association strength between two
categorical variables based on their observed vs. expected co-occurrence
frequencies. PMI quantifies how much more (or less) frequently two events
co-occur compared to what would be expected under statistical independence.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                                                                  | Default    |
|--------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| f12    | IntoExprColumn | Joint frequencies of variable pairs. Can be a column name (str) or Polars expression.        | _required_ |
| f1     | IntoExprColumn | Marginal frequencies of first variable. Can be a column name (str) or Polars expression.     | _required_ |
| f2     | IntoExprColumn | Marginal frequencies of second variable. Can be a column name (str) or Polars expression.    | _required_ |
| n      | IntoExprColumn | Grand total (total number of observations). Can be a column name (str) or Polars expression. | _required_ |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type    | Description                                                              |
|--------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | pl.Expr | A Polars expression that computes the PMI values for each variable pair. |

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

PMI is calculated as:

.. math::
    PMI(x,y) = \log\frac{P(x,y)}{P(x)P(y)} = \log\frac{f_{12} \cdot n}{f_1 \cdot f_2}
